counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence that renal infarction is the primary diagnosis
No alternative explanation for the LV mass
No disconfirming pathology for synovial sarcoma
decisive_items: Endomyocardial biopsies revealed a malignant spindle cell tumor, histology consistent with the monophasic variant
Trans-thoracic echocardiography (TTE) showed a large left ventricular (LV) mass
Cytogenetics by fluorescence in situ hybridization showed SS18 (SYT;18q11.2) translocation
response.rationale: R3 is supported by definitive pathology (malignant spindle cell tumor, monophasic variant) and imaging (LV mass) plus cytogenetic translocation, directly identifying cardiac synovial sarcoma. R1 only cites renal infarction, which is a secondary embolic manifestation of the cardiac mass, not the underlying diagnosis.

rejected.why: Renal infarction is a downstream complication of the cardiac mass, not the most likely primary diagnosis; lacks pathological or genetic confirmation.
